sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 (ms. dated 3 Dec 2012). An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. III. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 366 'Olulumọ–Ikọm cluster', printed p. 71.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives names (Òkúní; Òlúlùmọ; Ikọm), location (Ikom LGA), populations (9,250 in 1953; Olulumọ 1,730/5,000 Faraclas 1989; Ikọm 7,520/25,000), classification (Benue–Congo: Cross River: Delta–Cross: Upper Cross: Central: East–West) and one reference: 'Cook Benue–Congo Newsletter 6'. No phonology of any kind; the tone marks on the ethnonyms are the only prosodic information.
